record_type_quote:
The present study is a preregistered direct replication
of the cornerstone experimental study by D. Wood et al. (1978), who found empirical evidence for the claim
that a contingent use of verbal and nonverbal levels of instruction lies at the heart of scaffolding.

targets.authors: Wood, D., Wood, H., & Middleton, D.
targets.title: An experimental evaluation of four face-to-face teaching strategies.
targets.evidence_quote:
The present study is a preregistered direct replication
of the cornerstone experimental study by D. Wood et al. (1978), who found empirical evidence for the claim
that a contingent use of verbal and nonverbal levels of instruction lies at the heart of scaffolding.
targets.outcome_quote:
However, we
failed to replicate the positive effect of contingent instruction on
the children’s task success.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The central contingent-instruction advantage failed; replicated procedural characteristics do not establish success of the tested finding.

reasoning: New randomized sample directly retests the published 1978 experiment; the 1975 and 1976 descriptive studies and later conceptual replications are background.
